events.headline: FDA approves AMONDYS 45 (casimersen), Sarepta's third exon-skipping DMD drug
events.detail: The FDA approved AMONDYS 45 under accelerated approval, based on an increase in dystrophin production observed in patients amenable to exon 45 skipping, with continued approval contingent on verification of clinical benefit in confirmatory trials (the ESSENCE trial, then expected to conclude by 2024).

source.title: Sarepta Therapeutics Announces FDA Approval of AMONDYS 45 (casimersen) Injection for the Treatment of Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) in Patients Amenable to Skipping Exon 45

events.headline: Sarepta reports SRP-9001 expression and safety data using its commercial manufacturing process (Study 103/ENDEAVOR)
events.detail: In the first 11 participants of Study SRP-9001-103 (ENDEAVOR), the first trial to use Sarepta's commercially representative manufacturing material, micro-dystrophin expression reached 55.4% of normal by western blot at 12 weeks, and the company said the safety profile was consistent with prior studies with no new safety signals identified; two participants had serious adverse events (elevated liver enzymes in one, nausea/vomiting in another) that resolved.

source.title: Sarepta Therapeutics' Investigational Gene Therapy for the Treatment of Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy, SRP-9001, Demonstrates Robust Expression and Consistent Safety Profile Using Sarepta's Commercial Process Material

events.headline: Federal Reserve raises interest rates 75 basis points, the largest single hike since 1994
events.detail: The Federal Reserve raised the federal funds target range to 1.5%-1.75%. Connection to this business: Sarepta's gene-therapy program was, per the pre-cutoff packet, dependent on continued capital-markets access alongside product revenue and partner payments to fund development and manufacturing scale-up; 2022's rising-rate environment raised the general cost and scrutiny of capital raising for development-stage biotech spending, the backdrop against which Sarepta's September 2022 debt financing [e4] occurred.

source.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

events.headline: Sarepta issues $1.13 billion of convertible senior notes due 2027
events.detail: Sarepta issued $1.130 billion aggregate principal amount of 1.250% convertible senior notes due September 15, 2027 ($980.0 million to initial purchasers plus a fully exercised $150.0 million option, plus $20.0 million to an affiliated investor). It used part of the proceeds to repurchase $150.6 million of its 1.50% convertible notes due 2024 and to repay about $585.5 million of outstanding term loans.

source.title: Sarepta Therapeutics, Inc. Form 8-K (convertible notes offering)

events.headline: FDA grants accelerated approval to ELEVIDYS (SRP-9001) gene therapy for ambulatory patients aged 4-5
events.detail: The FDA approved ELEVIDYS (delandistrogene moxeparvovec) under accelerated approval for ambulatory DMD patients aged 4 through 5, based on micro-dystrophin expression, with continued approval contingent on verification of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial (the then-fully-enrolled Phase 3 EMBARK study).

source.title: Sarepta Therapeutics Announces FDA Approval of ELEVIDYS, the First Gene Therapy to Treat Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1)
source.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (EDGAR, Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1)

events.headline: EMBARK confirmatory trial misses primary NSAA endpoint but meets key secondary endpoints
events.detail: In the Phase 3 EMBARK study (ages 4-7), ELEVIDYS-treated patients improved 2.6 points on the NSAA total score at week 52 versus 1.9 points on placebo, a 0.65-point difference that was not statistically significant (p=0.24); all pre-specified key secondary endpoints, including time-to-rise and 10-meter walk test, were statistically significant in favor of treatment, and the company said no new safety signals were seen. The company said it planned to seek a label expansion based on the totality of the data, having discussed the results with FDA leadership.

source.title: Sarepta Therapeutics Announces Topline Results from EMBARK, a Global Pivotal Study of ELEVIDYS Gene Therapy for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy

events.headline: FDA expands ELEVIDYS approval to all DMD patients aged 4 and older
events.detail: The FDA expanded the ELEVIDYS indication to patients aged 4 and older with a confirmed DMD gene mutation, granting traditional approval for ambulatory individuals and accelerated approval (again contingent on a confirmatory trial) for non-ambulatory individuals.

source.title: Sarepta Therapeutics Announces Expanded US FDA Approval of ELEVIDYS to Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy Patients Ages 4 and Above

events.opened_note: No SEC 8-K exhibit matching this release could be located via EDGAR full-text search for this date range; a patient-advocacy-organization mirror of the company press release was used instead of the company's own investor-relations page, which repeatedly timed out.

events.headline: Sarepta discloses first death linked to ELEVIDYS, from acute liver failure; shares fall sharply
events.detail: Sarepta reported that a patient with DMD died of acute liver failure after ELEVIDYS treatment -- a severity of liver injury not previously reported for the therapy, which had by then treated more than 800 clinical and prescribed patients. The company noted the patient had a recent cytomegalovirus infection that the treating physician identified as a possible contributing factor, and said it still viewed the risk-benefit profile as positive.
events.source_quote: The company's stock plunged around 22% as the markets opened on Tuesday to $78.54, down from $101.35 at the previous market close.

source.title: Sarepta Shares Crash 22% After Patient on DMD Gene Therapy Elevidys Dies

events.opened_note: Sarepta's own community-letter announcement (sarepta.com, same date, same facts) was also opened; the BioSpace article is cited here because it explicitly links the disclosure to the same-day price move, which the company letter does not address.

events.headline: Sarepta discloses a second ELEVIDYS-linked death; halts dosing in ongoing gene-therapy trial and suspends 2025 revenue guidance
events.detail: Sarepta disclosed a second patient death, again attributed to acute liver failure following ELEVIDYS treatment. The company said it would pause dosing in the Phase 3 ENVISION trial, temporarily halt Elevidys shipments to non-ambulatory patients, assemble an independent expert group to consider an enhanced immunosuppression regimen (including possible addition of sirolimus), and suspend its full-year 2025 revenue guidance.
events.source_quote: Stock crashed 41% to $21.01 in premarket trading Monday morning following the announcement.

source.title: UPDATE: Second Patient Dies After Receiving Sarepta's DMD Gene Therapy Elevidys

events.opened_note: Article says the death was announced Sunday evening (2025-06-15) with the market reaction the following Monday morning; the article itself is dated 2025-06-16.

events.headline: Sarepta pauses all U.S. Elevidys shipments after an informal FDA request
events.detail: Several days after the FDA made an informal request on July 18, 2025 for Sarepta to voluntarily pause U.S. Elevidys shipments, Sarepta agreed to pause all shipments effective close of business July 22, 2025, having previously paused only shipments to non-ambulatory patients after the June death [e9]. The FDA subsequently recommended on July 28, 2025 that Sarepta resume shipments for ambulatory patients, while the pause for non-ambulatory patients continued pending further discussion.

source.title: Sarepta Voluntarily Pauses All Shipments of DMD Gene Therapy Elevidys Several Days After Informal Request From FDA

events.headline: FDA approves a boxed warning for ELEVIDYS and restricts the indication to ambulatory patients only
events.detail: The FDA approved a Boxed Warning -- its most prominent safety warning -- for the risk of serious liver injury and acute liver failure, including fatal outcomes, and revised the ELEVIDYS indication to cover only ambulatory patients aged 4 and older with a confirmed DMD mutation, removing the accelerated-approval indication for non-ambulatory patients granted in June 2024 [e7]. The FDA cited two reports of fatal acute liver failure in non-ambulatory pediatric patients (both hospitalized within two months of infusion) and one additional serious non-fatal liver-injury case, and is requiring a postmarketing observational study of about 200 patients followed for at least 12 months.

source.title: FDA Approves New Safety Warning and Revised Indication that Limits Use for Elevidys Following Reports of Fatal Liver Injury

horizon_notes.1: In the year after cutoff, both catalysts named in the pre-cutoff packet resolved close to their guided windows: the FDA approved the third exon-skipping drug, AMONDYS 45 (casimersen), on February 25, 2021, matching the packet's named decision deadline [e1], and Study 103 (ENDEAVOR) reported biomarker and safety data using the commercial manufacturing process in May 2021, in the second quarter as guided, with no new safety signals identified [e2]. Interpretation: the packet's two named catalysts both landed on schedule, an early signal that management's specific regulatory and manufacturing-transition claims were reliable; it contained no signal, however, about the gene-therapy safety concerns that emerged years later.
horizon_notes.3: By the third anniversary, the SRP-9001 gene therapy that had missed its primary functional endpoint at cutoff had received FDA accelerated approval as ELEVIDYS for ambulatory patients aged 4-5 in June 2023 [e5]; its EMBARK confirmatory trial then missed its own primary NSAA endpoint in October 2023 while meeting all key secondary endpoints [e6]; and the company financed the interim period with $1.13 billion of convertible notes in September 2022 rather than new equity [e4], against a backdrop of rising interest rates [e3]. Interpretation: the packet flagged the missed functional endpoint and the age-subgroup-only positive result as open questions about whether the effect was real and reproducible; the record through this anniversary shows the pattern repeating in a second, larger controlled trial (EMBARK), a data point the packet could not have contained since EMBARK had not yet been run.
horizon_notes.5: By the fifth anniversary, the safety picture had changed materially: Sarepta disclosed an ELEVIDYS-linked death from acute liver failure in March 2025 [e8], a second death in June 2025 that led it to pause gene-therapy trial dosing and suspend 2025 revenue guidance [e9], a full voluntary U.S. shipment pause in July 2025 after an FDA request, later partly lifted for ambulatory patients [e10], and in November 2025 an FDA-approved boxed warning with the indication narrowed back to ambulatory patients only [e11] -- reversing the non-ambulatory expansion granted in June 2024 [e7]. Interpretation: the pre-cutoff packet's 'short' column had already named serious adverse events, including liver-enzyme elevation, in 3 of the original 41 treated patients as a specific risk; the fifth-anniversary record shows a related risk recurring at a more severe, eventually fatal level in a larger post-approval population, though the packet could not have said in which patients or how the FDA's approved indication would later be narrowed in response.

aftermath.attribution_caveat: Price moves have many causes; the events here are what was public, not a proof of why the price moved.
gaps: Two of the press-release-sourced events (EMBARK topline, e6; the June 2024 label expansion, e7) could not be corroborated against a Sarepta-hosted or SEC-filed primary source in this pass: investorrelations.sarepta.com and businesswire.com repeatedly timed out or returned 403 errors, and EDGAR full-text search found no 8-K exhibit containing the expected keywords for either date range, despite both being clearly material events. Patient-advocacy-organization mirrors of the same press releases were used instead and are believed accurate but are one step removed from the company's own posting.

The FDA's July 28, 2025 recommendation to resume ambulatory shipments is mentioned only inside event e10's detail, sourced to the same July 22 article, and was not independently verified against a dedicated primary source for that specific date.

A third, non-Elevidys death (a 51-year-old limb-girdle muscular dystrophy patient in a Phase 1 trial of the related investigational gene therapy SRP-9004, reported around July 2025) was identified in secondary sources but not included as a dated event here, since it concerns a different drug program using the same AAV serotype rather than ELEVIDYS itself.

The 2024 Roche relationship and any specific milestone or royalty payments referenced generically in player.json's unresolved questions ('the partner's committed payments') were not independently researched for specific dated amounts in this pass.

This session's WebSearch tool budget was exhausted partway through this case's research (a session-wide cap, not specific to this case); the later events in this timeline (e8-e11) were sourced via WebFetch on URLs already surfaced by earlier searches, and via direct EDGAR full-text-search API calls through Bash rather than further WebSearch calls.

scene_check.voice: Gene therapy for muscular dystrophy misses its main functional goal in first placebo-controlled trial; company points to protein expression and a younger-patient subgroup.

claims.text: primary biological endpoint met (p<0.0001) and the 4-5 year subgroup significant
two approved drugs generate $121 million a quarter and cash is about $1.8 billion

debrief_check.s1: The miss was real and it repeated: the larger confirmatory trial also missed the same functional endpoint in October 2023, while meeting secondaries [e6].
debrief_check.s2: The subgroup carried the day with the regulator: accelerated approval for ages 4 to 5 in June 2023, expanded to all ages in 2024, then narrowed back after two liver-failure deaths and a boxed warning in 2025 [e5][e7][e8][e9][e11].
debrief_check.s3: The revenue base held and a third exon-skipping drug was approved on its deadline in February 2021; the company financed the gap with $1.13 billion of convertible notes rather than equity [e1][e4]. The packet's own 'short' column had named liver-enzyme elevation as a risk; it recurred at a fatal scale years later.

assumptions.text: The younger-patient subgroup result is real and will convince the regulator.
The functional miss means the therapy does not work; the market is right to sell.
The revenue base and cash make this a setback, not an existential event.
The safety findings will matter more than efficacy in the end.
I don't have enough evidence to take a position either way.

thesis_check.a1: Evidence: accelerated approval for ages 4 to 5 came in June 2023, then expansion to all ages in 2024, while the larger confirmatory trial again missed the same functional endpoint in October 2023 [e5][e6][e7]. For this assumption: right about the regulator, unproven about the biology. Unknown: what the functional benefit is; two trials have not shown it in the full population.
thesis_check.a2: Evidence: the therapy reached the market on a surrogate endpoint and expanded, before deaths and a boxed warning narrowed it again in 2025 [e5][e7][e8][e11]. For this assumption: the miss did not stop approval within three years; whether it 'works' is still contested at five. Unknown: long-term function in treated boys.
thesis_check.a3: Evidence: the third drug was approved on its deadline, revenue kept coming, and the company financed itself with $1.13 billion of convertible notes rather than equity [e1][e4]. For this assumption: supported through the three-year horizon. Unknown: the 2025 safety crisis, which suspended revenue guidance [e9].
thesis_check.a4: Evidence: the packet's three serious events included liver-enzyme elevation; in 2025 two patients died of acute liver failure, shipments were paused and a boxed warning was added [e8][e9][e10][e11]. For this assumption: not visible inside three years, decisive at five. Unknown: whether the signal in 41 patients was readable as the later risk; the record only shows the recurrence.
thesis_check.a5: Evidence: a mixed readout became an approval, then a confirmatory miss, then a safety reversal [e5][e6][e8]. For this assumption: fair; each stop reversed the previous one. Unknown: any horizon shorter than five years tells a different story than the full one.

baseline.narrative: Your window ends before the third exon-skipping drug's approval decision or any gene-therapy trial follow-up. The starting record leaves both the subgroup finding and the funding question unresolved.

checks.a1: Unresolved. The favorable subgroup result comes from one pre-specified cut of a 41-patient trial that did not reach significance in the full population; the starting record cannot establish whether it is reproducible or how the regulator will read it.
checks.a2: Unresolved. One controlled trial's non-significant primary endpoint, with the company citing an arm imbalance not independently confirmed, is not enough on its own to establish that the therapy does not work.
checks.a3: Unresolved. Revenue was growing but the third quarter alone was a $238 million cash outflow; the starting record cannot establish whether revenue and cash will cover the gene-therapy program without further financing.
checks.a4: Unresolved. Three of 41 treated patients had serious adverse events, including liver-enzyme elevation, in a therapy intended for children; the starting record cannot establish whether safety or efficacy will prove decisive.
checks.a5: Unresolved. The starting record contains a mixed clinical readout, approved sibling drugs on a surrogate endpoint, and an unresolved financing question, with no way yet to weigh them against each other.

updates.narrative: The regulator approved the third exon-skipping drug on its guided deadline, and early data using the planned commercial manufacturing process showed no new safety signals, though one of eleven participants again had elevated liver enzymes.

checks.a3: Partly supported. The FDA approved the third exon-skipping drug, AMONDYS 45, on its guided deadline, adding to the revenue base independent of the gene-therapy program. This does not establish that revenue and cash will cover future financing needs.
checks.a4: Unresolved. Early data using the commercial manufacturing process reported no new safety signals, but one of eleven participants again had elevated liver enzymes, echoing the earlier signal. Too few patients to show whether safety will prove decisive.

updates.narrative: The company issued $1.13 billion of convertible notes due 2027. About $736 million of the proceeds repaid earlier convertible notes and term loans, so the new money added was well below the headline amount.

checks.a3: Partly supported. The company issued $1.13 billion of convertible notes and used about $736 million of it to repay earlier notes and term loans; the rest added to cash. Access to debt markets does not show the business can carry that debt or fund development from revenue.

updates.narrative: The FDA granted accelerated approval for ambulatory patients aged 4 to 5, on the basis of micro-dystrophin expression, a surrogate measure, with the larger confirmatory trial still pending.

checks.a1: Partly supported. The FDA granted accelerated approval for ambulatory patients aged 4 to 5, but on micro-dystrophin expression, a surrogate, not on the subgroup's functional result. Whether that functional result is real awaits the confirmatory trial.

updates.narrative: The larger confirmatory trial again missed its primary functional endpoint while meeting key secondary endpoints, repeating the pattern from the packet's trial in a bigger population; the approval stood.

checks.a1: Weakened. The confirmatory trial, run in a wider age group, again missed its primary functional endpoint, repeating the earlier pattern. Secondary endpoints favored treatment, so this does not settle whether the subgroup effect is real.
checks.a2: Mixed. The primary functional endpoint missed significance again, echoing the earlier trial, but key secondary endpoints favored treatment and the approval was not withdrawn. This does not establish either that the therapy works or that it does not.

updates.narrative: The FDA expanded approval to all patients aged 4 and older, granting traditional, not just accelerated, approval for ambulatory patients based on the totality of the data.

checks.a1: Supported so far. The FDA granted traditional approval for ambulatory patients aged 4 and up, moving beyond the accelerated, subgroup-only approval. This reflects the regulator's read of the totality of data, not independent proof of the functional effect.
checks.a2: Weakened. The regulator granted full traditional approval for ambulatory patients despite the earlier functional misses, judging the totality of the data favorably. This does not establish that the therapy works in every patient it was later given to.

updates.narrative: Two patients died of acute liver failure after treatment in the months that followed, leading the company to halt trial dosing and suspend its 2025 revenue guidance.

checks.a4: Supported so far. Two acute liver failure deaths in treated patients, following the earlier liver-enzyme signal, led to a halted trial and an independent expert review. This does not yet settle whether safety will outweigh the approvals already granted.
checks.a3: Weakened. The second death led the company to suspend its 2025 revenue guidance and pause shipments to some patients. That undercuts the assumption that revenue and cash could absorb a setback without disruption to the business itself.

updates.narrative: Sarepta paused all U.S. shipments after an FDA request, and the FDA later added a boxed warning for fatal liver injury and narrowed the approval back to ambulatory patients only, removing the 2024 non-ambulatory expansion.

checks.a1: Partly supported. Approval stands for ambulatory patients, which includes the younger subgroup, while the non-ambulatory indication was removed after fatal liver injuries in those patients. The subgroup's functional effect was never confirmed on a primary endpoint.
checks.a2: Partly supported. The FDA required a boxed warning for fatal liver injury and narrowed the label, a regulatory judgment that the risk-benefit balance had shifted for some patients. Ambulatory patients retain approval, so this is not a full withdrawal.
checks.a4: Supported so far. A boxed warning for fatal liver injury and a narrowed indication followed two deaths, a safety consequence that reached the label itself. Whether this outweighs the efficacy case over the full history is still not fully settled.
